#9782. Rate-Limited Game Worker Drains: FIFO Windows and Idempotency-Key Recovery

Draining a rate-limited game worker pool is a recovery problem before it is a queue-selection problem. A FIFO queue can suppress a duplicate for five minutes, but it cannot make a payment, inventory update, or match reward exactly once. My default is a standard queue with an idempotent consumer and a durable job key; use FIFO deduplication as a short-lived filter, not as the correctness boundary.

Short answer: keep the queue replaceable, persist an idempotency key before side effects, and choose FIFO only when a five-minute duplicate window helps operational recovery.

For a solo team, Infrai fits the narrow middle: its queue is available through one plain REST contract, and the same key can cover adjacent backend capabilities as the game grows. That breadth matters during a migration because the application can keep its own job schema while swapping the queue implementation behind a small adapter.

Imagine a game backend draining 200 workers after a regional throttle. Each job asks an external service to refresh a player's entitlement. A consumer can receive a message, time out after the external call, and receive the same message again. The queue has no way to know whether the side effect committed.

The useful contract is at-least-once delivery plus an idempotent handler. Compute a key from the external request or business object, then record it in a database or cache before completing the side effect. A unique constraint turns a retry into a read, while a status such as processing lets a recovery worker distinguish an unfinished attempt from a completed one. In a real drain, I would also retain the original request ID and provider response metadata for audit; that record is what makes a six-minute replay explainable when the FIFO filter has already expired, and it gives an operator a deliberate way to resume rather than clicking a redeliver button and hoping.

That ordering matters. If the process crashes after the API call but before the key is stored, a later delivery can still repeat the call. A transactional outbox can close the gap when the job is emitted from the same transaction as the game state change; it does not magically make the remote service transactional.

FIFO deduplication is useful for a burst: two publishes with the same deduplication identity inside five minutes can collapse before a worker sees both. The window expires. Longer protection belongs in the consumer's database or cache, with a retention policy that matches the business action rather than the queue setting.

For a rate-limited drain, I also cap concurrency in the worker and acknowledge only after the idempotent write and the external request have reached the intended state. A standard queue remains a good fit for many business apps because the consumer logic is explicit and the queue does not pretend to provide exactly-once execution.

Here is a compact TypeScript sketch using the queue surface. It keeps retries bounded, honors Retry-After, and sends an application idempotency key in the message. The durable claim operation is intentionally shown as a local boundary: its implementation belongs to your database or cache.

The exact request fields for your queue configuration should come from its discovery schema; the important design is the durable key and the post-processing acknowledgement. Keep queue retention at or below 30 days, and keep delayed messages at or below seven days. Those limits make a queue a poor replay log for analytics or multiple consumer groups.

The comparison axis here is recovery behavior, not a leaderboard of features.

Infrai is worth trying for a small team that wants the queue and other backend modules behind one plain REST API, so adding a capability does not add another SDK and credential flow. Its discovery surface is public and self-describing, with runnable examples for documented capabilities; that gives a migration adapter a concrete schema to target instead of a hand-written guess. The supporting breadth is real: 295 routes across 20 modules under one key. Infrai uses the same key, one wallet, and one bill for queue, storage, and observability work, so those adapters do not create separate credential and reconciliation chores. Because the contract stays uniform, switching a provider later can leave the worker's business code unchanged while only the adapter moves.

The catch is important: choose RabbitMQ or a workflow system such as Temporal when you need long-running orchestration, fan-out joins, or replay streams. Choose SQS when deep AWS-native integration is the priority. Choose BullMQ when Redis is already your operational center. Infrai does not support those workflow and replay shapes, and its cron trigger is limited to 900 seconds; long work should be cron-triggered into a queue and drained by workers.

Run a failure-injection check around the external side effect: kill a worker after the remote request returns, replay the same message after six minutes, and let the rate limiter reject a burst. Record duplicate side effects, time-to-recovery, age of the idempotency record, and the number of messages that reach a dead-letter path. I am not sure your provider's retry timing will match these examples, so test the actual policy rather than copying a default.

The decision rule is simple. If the business key can be stored durably and the worker can safely retry, standard at-least-once delivery is usually enough. Add FIFO when its ordering and five-minute suppression reduce noise during a drain. Never promote that filter into an exactly-once promise. If this boundary fits your system, start with the queue capability guide and keep the adapter small.

Are you looking for a new graphic design tool? Would you like to read a detailed review of Canva? As it's one of the tools I love using. I am also writing my first ebook using canva and publish it soon on my site you can download it is free.  Let's start the review.

Canva has a web version and also a mobile app

Canva is a free graphic design web application that allows you to create invitations, business cards, flyers, lesson plans, banners, and more using professionally designed templates. You can upload your own photos from your computer or from Google Drive, and add them to Canva's templates using a simple drag-and-drop interface. It's like having a basic version of Photoshop that doesn't require Graphic designing knowledge to use. It’s best for nongraphic designers.

Canva is a great tool for small business owners, online entrepreneurs, and marketers who don’t have the time and want to edit quickly.

To create sophisticated graphics, a tool such as Photoshop can is ideal. To use it, you’ll need to learn its hundreds of features, get familiar with the software, and it’s best to have a good background in design, too.

Also running the latest version of Photoshop you need a high-end computer.

So here  Canva takes place, with Canva you can do all that with drag-and-drop feature. It’s also easier to use and free. Also an even-more-affordable paid version is available for $12.95 per month.

The product is available in three plans: Free, Pro ($12.99/month per user or  $119.99/year for up to 5 people), and Enterprise ($30 per user per month, minimum 25 people).

To get started on Canva, you will need to create an account by providing your email address, Google, Facebook or Apple credentials. You will then choose your account type between student, teacher, small business, large company, non-profit, or personal. Based on your choice of account type, templates will be recommended to you.

You can sign up for a free trial of Canva Pro, or you can start with the free version to get a sense of whether it’s the right graphic design tool for your needs.

When you sign up for an account, Canva will suggest different post types to choose from. Based on the type of account you set up  you'll be able to see templates categorized by the following categories: social media posts, documents, presentations, marketing, events, ads, launch your business, build your online brand, etc.

Start by choosing a template for your post or searching for something more specific. Search by social network name to see a list of post types on each network.

Next, you can choose a template. Choose from hundreds of templates that are ready to go, with customizable photos, text, and other elements.

You can start your design by choosing from a variety of ready-made templates, searching for a template matching your needs, or working with a blank template.

Inside the Canva designer, the Elements tab gives you access to lines and shapes, graphics, photos, videos, audio, charts, photo frames, and photo grids.The search box on the Elements tab lets you search everything on Canva.

To begin with, Canva has a large library of elements to choose from. To find them, be specific in your search query. You may also want to search in the following tabs to see various elements separately:

The Photos tab lets you search for and choose from millions of professional stock photos for your templates.

You can replace the photos in our templates to create a new look. This can also make the template more suited to your industry.

You can find photos on other stock photography sites like pexel, pixabay and many more or simply upload your own photos.

When you choose an image, Canva’s photo editing features let you adjust the photo’s settings (brightness, contrast, saturation, etc.), crop, or animate it.

The Text tab lets you add headings, normal text, and graphical text to your design.

When you click on  text, you'll see options to adjust the font, font size, color, format, spacing, and text effects (like shadows).

Create an animated image or video by adding audio to capture user’s attention in social news feeds.

If you want to use audio from another stock site or your own audio tracks, you can upload them in the Uploads tab or from the more option.

Want to create your own videos? Choose from thousands of stock video clips. You’ll find videos that range upto 2 minutes

You can upload your own videos as well as videos from other stock sites in the Uploads tab.

Once you have chosen a video, you can use the editing features in Canva to trim the video, flip it, and adjust its transparency.

On the Background tab, you’ll find free stock photos to serve as backgrounds on your designs. Change out the background on a template to give it a more personal touch.

The Styles tab lets you quickly change the look and feel of your template with just a click. And if you have a Canva Pro subscription, you can upload your brand’s custom colors and fonts to ensure designs stay on brand.

If you have a Canva Pro subscription, you’ll have a Logos tab. Here, you can upload variations of your brand logo to use throughout your designs.

With Canva, you can also create your own logos. Note that you cannot trademark a logo with stock content in it.

With Canva, free users can download and share designs to multiple platforms including Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Slack and Tumblr.

Canva Pro allows you to work with your team on visual content. Designs can be created inside Canva, and then sent to your team members for approval. Everyone can make comments, edits, revisions, and keep track via the version history.

When it comes to printing your designs, Canva has you covered. With an extensive selection of printing options, they can turn your designs into anything from banners and wall art to mugs and t-shirts.

Canva Print is perfect for any business seeking to make a lasting impression. Create inspiring designs people will want to wear, keep, and share. Hand out custom business cards that leave a lasting impression on customers' minds.

The Canva app is available on the Apple App Store and Google Play. The Canva app has earned a 4.9 out of five star rating from over 946.3K Apple users and a 4.5 out of five star rating from over 6,996,708 Google users.

In addition to mobile apps, you can use Canva’s integration with other Internet services to add images and text from sources like Google Maps, Emojis, photos from Google Drive and Dropbox, YouTube videos, Flickr photos, Bitmojis, and other popular visual content elements.

In general, Canva is an excellent tool for those who need simple images for projects. If you are a graphic designer with experience, you will find Canva’s platform lacking in customization and advanced features – particularly vectors. But if you have little design experience, you will find Canva easier to use than advanced graphic design tools like Adobe Photoshop or Illustrator for most projects. #9778. Three Philippine Agencies Shipped AI Education Rules in One School Year. The Proof Is Still Being Assembled.

Posted on Nov 12 • Originally published at yanoai.tech

CHED's Memorandum Order No. 21 set a national framework for AI in higher education covering 2,366 institutions (Source: CHED, 2026). Within roughly one school year, DepEd launched the country's first nationwide AI program for basic education, and TESDA opened free AI courses. What has not arrived is the measurement layer that would show whether any of it changed how Filipino students actually learn.

That condition will be the hardest to audit. "Strengthens rather than replaces" is not a metric any HEI reports, and no national baseline exists for it. A rule can be written in a semester. Proving it changed behavior takes years.

DepEd launched AGAP.AI (Accelerating Governance and Adaptive Pedagogy through Artificial Intelligence) on January 9, 2026, described as the Philippines' first nationwide program for responsible AI integration in basic education (Source: DepEd and Microsoft, 2026). It targets AI literacy and ethical use training for 1.5 million students, teachers and parents. The DepEd system it operates inside covers more than 24 million students.

Here is the ratio: 1.5 million people targeted for training against more than 24 million students, roughly one in sixteen.

DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara named the reason: "Literacy remains one of our biggest national challenges, with many learners still not meeting expected proficiency levels" (Source: DepEd and Microsoft, 2026).

The clearest numbers come from ARAL, the Academic Recovery and Accessible Learning program launched in September 2025 (Source: DepEd and Microsoft, 2026). Under it, Microsoft has begun enabling educators in 25 school districts and targets 3,000 teachers across 1,500 schools throughout 2026.

Early literacy data is promising but local. Microsoft Reading Progress has assessed over 14,000 learners in 61 schools in Bais and Dumaguete, and in Cabanatuan City, 100% of learners in 3 school districts progressed to higher literacy levels (Source: DepEd and Microsoft, 2026).

Sixty-one schools is a good start and a small sample. A national AI literacy figure needs the whole school system as the evaluation surface.

TESDA partnered with UNESCO-UNEVOC and the HP Foundation to place HP LIFE courses on the TESDA Online Program, the national e-learning platform (Source: UNESCO, 2026). The catalog covers AI concepts, responsible AI use, entrepreneurship, marketing and finance. Every course is free and delivered online, so access depends on connectivity rather than enrollment paperwork.

The ambition behind the channel is larger than one country. The UNESCO Global Skills Academy, which carries those courses, has committed to supporting ten million youth and adults globally in building essential skills by 2029 (Source: UNESCO, 2026).

Philippine edtech grew from USD 1.1 billion in 2025 to USD 1.3 billion in 2026, and is projected to reach USD 2.9 billion by 2034 at a compound annual growth rate of 10.87% (Source: IMARC Group, 2026).

IMARC Group cites demand for digital learning platforms, career-focused tech training, investment in AI and Web3 education, and policy-driven digital tools among the drivers (Source: IMARC Group, 2026). Note the last one. Vendors are pricing the memorandum orders as demand, and when policy moves ahead of measurement, forecasts move faster than evidence.

For providers the arithmetic runs in reverse. A company like Yano.AI, which builds AI-assisted learning products for Philippine schools and enterprises, does not sell against a market estimate. It sells against one classroom's adoption rate at a time, and the only honest proof is usage data from the schools themselves.

None of this requires new legislation, only budget lines and reporting discipline the agencies now have the mandate to create.

Q: Has the Philippines actually regulated AI in schools? A: Yes, at the policy level, across three agencies. CHED's Memorandum Order No. 21 governs AI in 2,366 higher education institutions (Source: CHED, 2026). DepEd's AGAP.AI governs responsible AI integration in basic education (Source: DepEd and Microsoft, 2026). TESDA channels free AI and digital skills courses through its national e-learning platform (Source: UNESCO, 2026).

Q: How many Filipino students are being trained in AI literacy? A: AGAP.AI targets 1.5 million students, teachers and parents in AI literacy and ethical use, against a DepEd system covering more than 24 million students (Source: DepEd and Microsoft, 2026). Roughly one in sixteen.

Q: Is AI training in the Philippines free? A: The TESDA channel is. HP LIFE courses on the TESDA Online Program are free and delivered online, and the UNESCO Global Skills Academy behind them targets ten million youth and adults globally by 2029 (Source: UNESCO, 2026).

Q: How large is the Philippine edtech market? A: It grew from USD 1.1 billion in 2025 to USD 1.3 billion in 2026, and is projected to reach USD 2.9 billion by 2034 at a 10.87% compound annual growth rate (Source: IMARC Group, 2026).

The Philippines shipped AI rules and programs from three agencies within one school year, across 2,366 higher education institutions, more than 24 million basic education students, and an open channel of free courses (Source: CHED, 2026; Source: DepEd and Microsoft, 2026; Source: UNESCO, 2026).

The one in sixteen coverage ratio and the 61 schools of assessment data are not reasons to slow down. They are a spec for what to build next, and most of it needs no new law.

So the question for every school, division and vendor is simple: if your AI contribution never appears in a national or regional dataset, can you still claim it worked? What would it take for your classrooms to be counted in the next AI literacy baseline?

#9776. I Used AI Coding Tools for 30 Days. Here’s What Made Me Faster (And What Didn’t)

Content writer exploring business, technology, AI, digital marketing, trends, and current affairs. Sharing insights and ideas that matter.

Content writer exploring business, technology, AI, digital marketing, trends, and current affairs. Sharing insights and ideas that matter.

Content writer exploring business, technology, AI, digital marketing, trends, and current affairs. Sharing insights and ideas that matter.

A few weeks ago, I caught myself spending 40 minutes writing a form validation schema I had written a dozen times before. I wasn’t learning anything. I was just typing.

That was the moment I decided to run an experiment: for 30 days, I would use AI coding assistants on every project I touched, and I would log what saved me time and what quietly wasted it.

I expected a magic productivity boost. What I got was more nuanced. Some habits made me noticeably faster. Others made me slower while feeling productive, which is the worst combination.

This is the honest breakdown, including the mistakes.

I mostly build web apps with React and Node.js, with the occasional Python script for automation. During the experiment, I worked on three things:

I used ChatGPT, Claude, and GitHub Copilot alongside VS Code. To keep myself honest, I kept a plain notes file with three columns: the task, my estimate without help, and the actual time taken. It isn’t scientific, but it was enough to spot patterns.

The biggest win was boilerplate: config files, validation, CRUD endpoints, regex, date formatting. I know exactly what I want in these tasks, but typing them out is tedious.

Here is a real example. I needed to validate a signup request. Writing it by hand meant checking the docs for the right syntax, handling each field and then writing error messages. About 15 minutes.

“Express 4, Node 20. Write a validation middleware for a signup route using Joi. Fields: name (2-50 chars), email, password (min 8, at least one number). Return 400 with a clear message for each failure.”

I got a working first draft in under a minute, reviewed it, tweaked two messages and moved on. Total: about 3 minutes.

The rule I settled on: if I can explain the task in two sentences and I’d be bored writing it, hand it off.

My early prompts were lazy: “fix this error.” The answers were generic and often wrong.

Then I started including four things every time:

“I’m using Express 4 with Node 20. This POST route returns a 500 when the body is empty. Here’s the handler and the error log. I expect a 400 with a validation message.”

The second one gets a useful answer on the first try almost every time. Good prompting turned out to be the same skill as writing a good bug report, and that skill makes you a better teammate even without any tools.

This surprised me the most. When I joined the older codebase, I pasted unfamiliar functions and asked, “Explain what this does, what its inputs are and what could break it.”

I still read the code myself afterwards, but having a first explanation to check against cut my onboarding time from what I estimated would be a week to about three days. It also helped me find a function that silently swallowed errors, which nobody on the team knew about.

I’m not great at imagining how my own code will fail. Asking for “10 edge cases for this function that might break it” gave me inputs I wouldn’t have tried: empty arrays, null values, unicode characters, extremely large numbers, duplicate entries.

Three of those edge cases exposed real bugs in a date-range function I thought was finished.

Explaining a bug to someone often solves it. These tools work like a duck that talks back. Half the time, I found the answer while typing out the question. The other half, the reply pointed me in the right direction.

In week two, I accepted a generated function without a careful review. It looked clean and passed my quick test. It also had an off-by-one error that affected pagination, and it took me almost an hour to track down two days later.

Generated code sounds confident even when it’s wrong. Now I treat it like a pull request from a junior developer: useful, but it always needs review.

When I asked for an entire module in one prompt, the result was messy, inconsistent and hard to modify. Naming didn’t match my project, error handling was different in every file and some parts duplicated logic that already existed.

Smaller pieces worked far better: one function, one component, one query at a time.

This was the hidden cost. When I jumped straight to prompting, I skipped the design thinking. I ended up with code that worked but didn’t fit the rest of the system, and I paid for it later during refactoring.

Now I spend five minutes writing the approach in plain text before opening any tool: what the inputs are, what the output is, where the code will live. It saves far more time than it costs.

When I was learning a new concept (database indexing, in my case), copying answers meant I didn’t actually learn anything. A week later, I couldn’t reproduce it without help.

For learning, I now ask for hints and explanations, then try to write the solution myself first.

A few times, I got suggestions that used library methods which don’t exist or were removed in newer versions. The code looked perfectly reasonable. It simply failed at runtime.

Anything version-sensitive now gets checked against the official documentation.

A net gain of roughly 14 hours over a month. That is real, but it’s much smaller than the hype suggests, and it only came from using the tools deliberately, not constantly. The weeks where I used them for everything were not my most productive weeks.

After 30 days, this is the routine that stuck:

If you’re just starting out, be careful. These tools can make you feel like you understand something when you don’t. Use them to explain, to give hints and to review your code, not to skip the struggle that builds skill.

If you’re experienced, the value is in removing friction: the repetitive work, the first draft, the edge-case checklist. Your judgment is still the part that matters, and no tool replaces it.

These tools don’t replace understanding. They reward developers who already know what they want and can judge the result.

The people getting the most out of them aren’t the ones who use them the most. They’re the ones who know exactly when to use them, and when to close the tab and think.

If you try your own 30-day experiment, I’d love to hear what you find. What worked for you, and what quietly wasted your time?

#9773. Come far leggere a Claude Code i check di GitNest e proporre un nuovo tentativo che approvi tu in osFoundry

Alla fine di questa guida puoi chiedere a Claude Code "il change set di checkout è verde?" e ricevere una risposta letta da osFoundry, non indovinata dai tuoi test locali. Claude Code elenca i check sul commit composto del change set, ti dice quale è fallito e, se sembra instabile (flaky), richiede un nuovo tentativo solo per quel check. Il retry non parte quando lo chiede Claude Code. Arriva in osFoundry come scheda "Retry GitNest check" con la versione del change set e il commit esatto, e viene eseguito solo quando fai clic su Approve retry.

La CLI di osFoundry stampa la stessa riga con osfoundry agent connect claude --print. In Claude Code esegui /mcp, scegli osfoundry e poi Authenticate. Il browser apre osFoundry e scegli un workspace. Da lì gli strumenti compaiono come mcp__osfoundry__….

Un check mai eseguito non si può né leggere né ritentare. In GitNest apri la pagina delle impostazioni del repository. Qui contano due pannelli:

In GitNest, la sezione Project del repository dice "Connected agents in this project can use approved GitNest read tools when their connection owner still has repository access." Solo il proprietario del repository vede il selettore. Scegli un progetto e osFoundry conferma "Repository project updated".

Poi apri l'icona della chiave → Connected, seleziona la connessione di Claude Code e, sotto Projects, aggiungila a quel progetto.

Esempio: Aggiunta della connessione di Claude Code al progetto che contiene il repository

Sotto Tools, nello stesso pannello, "All supported tools are on by default." Quelli usati in questa guida compaiono come list gitnest work, list gitnest checks, list gitnest saved results, read gitnest work e propose gitnest check rerun. Per lasciare a Claude Code la sola lettura dei check, togli la spunta a propose gitnest check rerun e fai clic su Save tools.

I nomi di strumenti e argomenti sono quelli che il server di osFoundry restituisce da tools/list. Repository, change set, ID, nomi dei check e risposte sono contenuti di esempio.

Claude Code chiede conferma prima della chiamata propose perché lo strumento è annotato con destructiveHint: true. È la sua richiesta di permesso, separata dall'approvazione in osFoundry.

Prima di approvare, guarda il change set. Nella sua pagina di revisione in GitNest, il pannello dei check sta sopra le schede e riassume il commit composto in una riga, qui "Checks did not pass: e2e", con ogni check e il suo stato sotto. Un change set non ancora composto non mostra alcun pannello, e un commit senza check mostra "No checks have run against this commit" invece di una spunta.

La campanella mostra " proposes retrying a GitNest check". In icona della chiave → Connected → la tua connessione → Needs your approval, la scheda riporta:

Esempio: Una proposta Retry GitNest check sotto Needs your approval

"Review change set before approving" apre la stessa pagina di revisione. Se il commit sulla scheda è quello che hai controllato, fai clic su Approve retry. Il check e2e torna in coda per quel commit e il tuo runner lo prende in carico. Poi avvisa Claude Code, che richiama list_gitnest_checks.

Il retry indica un commit, non un branch. propose_gitnest_check_rerun richiede expected_change_set_version e expected_composition_oid, quindi la scheda dice sempre quale commit composto Claude Code ha visto fallire. Se qualcuno ricompone il change set mentre la scheda è in attesa, il commit che approveresti non è più quello sulla scheda. osFoundry ricontrolla versione, commit e stato del check al clic, e una scheda non aggiornata non viene eseguita. Il pannello mostra allora "Could not decide this proposal. Its access may have changed." Chiedi a Claude Code di rileggere i check e di proporre sul nuovo commit.

Si può ritentare solo un check concluso. La descrizione dello strumento dice "retry one finished check", e lo stato del check fa parte del ricontrollo. Un check già di nuovo in coda o in esecuzione, perché qualcun altro l'ha ritentato o il change set è stato ricomposto, non viene messo in coda una seconda volta.

Un check per proposta. check_name è una sola stringa di massimo 200 caratteri. Ritentare l'intera suite richiede una scheda per check, ognuna decisa da te. Così il retry di un e2e instabile non rilancia di nascosto una scansione di sicurezza che preferisci lasciare fallita.

In questo percorso niente gira sulle macchine di osFoundry né modifica il codice. I check girano sui runner che hai registrato. Approvare un retry rimette in coda un check, e basta. Non ricompone, non fa merge e non pubblica. Il merge aspetta comunque che ogni check obbligatorio passi sul commit.

Le letture restano essenziali. list_gitnest_checks restituisce uno stato limitato solo per il commit composto attuale. list_gitnest_saved_results e read_gitnest_work escludono i binding locali e le credenziali, quindi Claude Code può dirti che un test è fallito, ma non vede mai il token del runner né il percorso del tuo checkout locale.

Per provarlo, registra un runner su una macchina libera, fai push di un change set con un check che sai essere instabile e chiedi a Claude Code se è verde. La pagina di GitNest mostra le schermate di repository, change set e check, e la pagina Connected descrive il pannello di approvazione.

#9772. How I Made a 400-Page Storefront Load in Under a Second

I run a small e-commerce storefront — an online vape shop in Dubai with about 170 products, 37 categories, and 420 URLs in the sitemap. It is built with Next.js 16, Supabase, and Cloudinary, and it runs on the Vercel free plan, which means every deployment and every CPU second counts. Here is what actually moved the needle on speed, and what did not.

Before the change, a product page took 1.3–1.6 seconds just to show the product name, 2.1–2.3 seconds for the buy box, and 4–5.3 seconds total on a slow connection, at 364KB. The page was server-rendered on every visit: product data, reviews, and related products all fetched per request. On a free plan, that is both slow and expensive.

The single biggest win was generateStaticParams on the product and category pages. All 405 static pages now build in about 32 seconds, and a visit serves a pre-rendered page. Measured after the change: product name and buy box arrive with the first byte, TTFB 0.58–0.69s, total 0.79–0.91s, 246KB. Same content, same URLs — the work just moved from request time to build time.

Pre-rendering creates a second problem: when an admin edits a price, the stale page keeps serving. The fix was per-item cache tags — every loader tags exactly what it returns (product-, category-), and every admin save revalidates only the tags it touched, plus the page path. Changing one product's price refreshes that product's page and the category cards showing it, and nothing else.

One bug worth naming: the original code called revalidateTag after the return statement in three admin upsert functions, so it was dead code and admin edits never invalidated anything. The fix was moving the calls before the return. If your admin edits seem to "not take effect", check for code after a return before blaming the cache.

The checkout reserves stock before creating the order: a live read plus a conditional update on stock_qty (three retries per item), so two simultaneous orders cannot sell the same last unit. Over-ordering returns a 409 with a plain message. Cancelling or deleting an order restores exactly the reserved stock. When stock hits zero, the revalidation above flips the product page to "Out of Stock" on its own.

Product reviews used to load after the product. Loading them in parallel with the product (one Promise.all) cut a waterfall. New customer reviews are inserted with is_approved = false and only appear publicly after an admin approves them; the product's average rating is recomputed from approved reviews only. Nothing about this is clever — it is just doing the obvious thing in the right order.

The homepage is the slowest page on the site (426KB of HTML, 94 images) and the only real lever is cutting content — which the shop owner will not do, because the content is the SEO. The honest answer was to leave it alone and say so, rather than burn the free-plan budget on marginal gains. Not every slow page has a fix you are allowed to ship.

The live site is POD Shop, and the Juul range I used as the test case is at podshopdubai.com/category/juul. Same stack, same content — just faster, because the work happens at build time instead of on every visit.

#9769. Ahrefs vs SEMrush: Which SEO Tool Should You Use?

SEMrush and Ahrefs are among the most popular tools in the SEO industry. Both companies have been in business for years and have thousands of customers per month.

If you're a professional SEO or trying to do digital marketing on your own, at some point you'll likely consider using a tool to help with your efforts. Ahrefs and SEMrush are two names that will likely appear on your shortlist.

In this guide, I'm going to help you learn more about these SEO tools and how to choose the one that's best for your purposes.

SEMrush is a popular SEO tool with a wide range of features—it's the leading competitor research service for online marketers. SEMrush's SEO Keyword Magic tool offers over 20 billion Google-approved keywords, which are constantly updated and it's the largest keyword database.

The program was developed in 2007 as SeoQuake is a small Firefox extension

Ahrefs is a leading SEO platform that offers a set of tools to grow your search traffic, research your competitors, and monitor your niche. The company was founded in 2010, and it has become a popular choice among SEO tools. Ahrefs has a keyword index of over 10.3 billion keywords and offers accurate and extensive backlink data updated every 15-30 minutes and it is the world's most extensive backlink index database.

Now that you know a little more about each tool, let's take a look at how they compare. I'll analyze each tool to see how they differ in interfaces, keyword research resources, rank tracking, and competitor analysis.

Ahrefs and SEMrush both offer comprehensive information and quick metrics regarding your website's SEO performance. However, Ahrefs takes a bit more of a hands-on approach to getting your account fully set up, whereas SEMrush's simpler dashboard can give you access to the data you need quickly.

In this section, we provide a brief overview of the elements found on each dashboard and highlight the ease with which you can complete tasks.

The Ahrefs dashboard is less cluttered than that of SEMrush, and its primary menu is at the very top of the page, with a search bar designed only for entering URLs.

Additional features of the Ahrefs platform include:

When you log into the SEMrush Tool, you will find four main modules. These include information about your domains, organic keyword analysis, ad keyword, and site traffic.

Both Ahrefs and SEMrush have user-friendly dashboards, but Ahrefs is less cluttered and easier to navigate. On the other hand, SEMrush offers dozens of extra tools, including access to customer support resources.

When deciding on which dashboard to use, consider what you value in the user interface, and test out both.

If you're looking to track your website's search engine ranking, rank tracking features can help. You can also use them to monitor your competitors.

Let's take a look at Ahrefs vs. SEMrush to see which tool does a better job.

The Ahrefs Rank Tracker is simpler to use. Just type in the domain name and keywords you want to analyze, and it spits out a report showing you the search engine results page (SERP) ranking for each keyword you enter.

Rank Tracker looks at the ranking performance of keywords and compares them with the top rankings for those keywords. Ahrefs also offers:

You'll see metrics that help you understand your visibility, traffic, average position, and keyword difficulty.

It gives you an idea of whether a keyword would be profitable to target or not.

SEMRush offers a tool called Position Tracking. This tool is a project tool—you must set it up as a new project. Below are a few of the most popular features of the SEMrush Position Tracking tool:

The platform provides opportunities to track several SERP features, including Local tracking.

Intuitive reports allow you to track statistics for the pages on your website, as well as the keywords used in those pages.

Identify pages that may be competing with each other using the Cannibalization report.

Ahrefs is a more user-friendly option. It takes seconds to enter a domain name and keywords. From there, you can quickly decide whether to proceed with that keyword or figure out how to rank better for other keywords.

SEMrush allows you to check your mobile rankings and ranking updates daily, which is something Ahrefs does not offer. SEMrush also offers social media rankings, a tool you won't find within the Ahrefs platform. Both are good which one do you like let me know in the comment.

Keyword research is closely related to rank tracking, but it's used for deciding which keywords you plan on using for future content rather than those you use now.

When it comes to SEO, keyword research is the most important thing to consider when comparing the two platforms.

The Ahrefs Keyword Explorer provides you with thousands of keyword ideas and filters search results based on the chosen search engine.

Ahrefs supports several features, including:

SEMrush's Keyword Magic Tool has over 20 billion keywords for Google. You can type in any keyword you want, and a list of suggested keywords will appear.

Both of these tools offer keyword research features and allow users to break down complicated tasks into something that can be understood by beginners and advanced users alike.

If you're interested in keyword suggestions, SEMrush appears to have more keyword suggestions than Ahrefs does. It also continues to add new features, like the Keyword Gap tool and SERP Questions recommendations.

Both platforms offer competitor analysis tools, eliminating the need to come up with keywords off the top of your head. Each tool is useful for finding keywords that will be useful for your competition so you know they will be valuable to you.

Ahrefs' domain comparison tool lets you compare up to five websites (your website and four competitors) side-by-side.it also shows you how your site is ranked against others with metrics such as backlinks, domain ratings, and more.

Use the Competing Domains section to see a list of your most direct competitors, and explore how many keywords matches your competitors have.

To find more information about your competitor, you can look at the Site Explorer and Content Explorer tools and type in their URL instead of yours.

SEMrush provides a variety of insights into your competitors' marketing tactics. The platform enables you to research your competitors effectively. It also offers several resources for competitor analysis including:

Traffic Analytics helps you identify where your audience comes from, how they engage with your site, what devices visitors use to view your site, and how your audiences overlap with other websites.

SEMrush's Organic Research examines your website's major competitors and shows their organic search rankings, keywords they are ranking for, and even if they are ranking for any (SERP) features and more.

The Market Explorer search field allows you to type in a domain and lists websites or articles similar to what you entered. Market Explorer also allows users to perform in-depth data analytics on These companies and markets.

SEMrush wins here because it has more tools dedicated to competitor analysis than Ahrefs. However, Ahrefs offers a lot of functionality in this area, too. It takes a combination of both tools to gain an advantage over your competition.

When it comes to keyword data research, you will become confused about which one to choose.

Both tools are great. Choose the one which meets your requirements and if you have any experience using either Ahrefs or SEMrush let me know in the comment section which works well for you.

#9767. Étiquette, contraste, clavier : trois défauts fréquents des formulaires

Posted on Nov 12 • Originally published at claren.fr

Une demande d’acte, une inscription, une commande : tout passe par un formulaire. Trois situations que l’on retrouve souvent, chacune reproductible sur votre propre site en une minute.

Le test. Cliquez dans un champ et commencez à écrire. Si le nom du champ disparaît, il n’était qu’un texte d’exemple.

Ce que cela change. Une personne qui revient sur le formulaire ne sait plus ce qu’elle a saisi où. Avec un lecteur d’écran, le champ peut être annoncé sans nom.

La correction. Une étiquette visible, placée au-dessus du champ, et associée à lui dans le code. Le texte d’exemple peut rester, en complément.

Le test. Relevez les couleurs réellement utilisées pour le texte et son fond, puis mesurez leur rapport avec un outil de contraste. Un examen visuel au soleil peut révéler une gêne, mais il ne permet pas de conclure au respect du seuil. Sur un dégradé ou une image, vérifiez les zones derrière le texte.

Ce que cela change. Les consignes et les erreurs sont précisément les textes qu’il faut lire pour finir. Une vision qui baisse avec l’âge suffit à les perdre.

La correction. Un rapport de contraste d’au moins 4,5 pour 1 entre le texte et son fond, pour les textes de taille courante. Cela se mesure avec un outil gratuit, page par page.

Le test. Posez la souris et avancez avec la touche Tab. Chaque élément atteint doit se voir. Si le focus disparaît, ou saute un bouton, quelqu’un ne pourra pas l’utiliser.

Ce que cela change. Les personnes qui naviguent au clavier, avec un contacteur ou avec un lecteur d’écran, dépendent de cet ordre et de ce repère visible.

La correction. Des éléments interactifs natifs, un ordre de tabulation qui suit la lecture, et un indicateur de focus visible qui n’est pas retiré par la feuille de style.

Ils repèrent des défauts, ils ne mesurent pas la conformité. Un audit selon le RGAA examine chaque critère sur un échantillon représentatif, avec des outils d’assistance. Ces trois tests sont un bon premier pas pour savoir si le sujet mérite d’être ouvert.

À lire ensuite : À quoi ressemble une fiche de correction.

Publié à l'origine sur claren.fr par Claren, cabinet d'audit d'accessibilité RGAA. Données ouvertes : Baromètre.

#9765. Sellfy Review 2022: How Good Is This Ecommerce Platform?

Are you searching for an ecomerce platform to help you build an online store and sell products?

In this Sellfy review, we'll talk about how this eCommerce platform can let you sell digital products while keeping full control of your marketing.

And the best part? Starting your business can be done in just five minutes.

Let us then talk about the Sellfy platform and all the benefits it can bring to your business.

Sellfy is an eCommerce solution that allows digital content creators, including writers, illustrators, designers, musicians, and filmmakers, to sell their products online. Sellfy provides a customizable storefront where users can display their digital products and embed "Buy Now" buttons on their website or blog. Sellfy product pages enable users to showcase their products from different angles with multiple images and previews from Soundcloud, Vimeo, and YouTube. Files of up to 2GB can be uploaded to Sellfy, and the company offers unlimited bandwidth and secure file storage. Users can also embed their entire store or individual project widgets in their site, with the ability to preview how widgets will appear before they are displayed.

Sellfy is a powerful e-commerce platform that helps you personalize your online storefront. You can add your logo, change colors, revise navigation, and edit the layout of your store. Sellfy also allows you to create a full shopping cart so customers can purchase multiple items. And Sellfy gives you the ability to set your language or let customers see a translated version of your store based on their location.

Sellfy gives you the option to host your store directly on its platform, add a custom domain to your store, and use it as an embedded storefront on your website. Sellfy also optimizes its store offerings for mobile devices, allowing for a seamless checkout experience.

Sellfy allows creators to host all their products and sell all of their digital products on one platform. Sellfy also does not place storage limits on your store but recommends that files be no larger than 5GB. Creators can sell both standard and subscription-based products in any file format that is supported by the online marketplace. Customers can purchase products instantly after making a purchase – there is no waiting period.

You can organize your store by creating your product categories, sorting by any characteristic you choose. Your title, description, and the image will be included on each product page. In this way, customers can immediately evaluate all of your products. You can offer different pricing options for all of your products, including "pay what you want," in which the price is entirely up to the customer. This option allows you to give customers control over the cost of individual items (without a minimum price) or to set pricing minimums—a good option if you're in a competitive market or when you have higher-end products. You can also offer set prices per product as well as free products to help build your store's popularity.

Sellfy is ideal for selling digital content, such as ebooks. But it does not allow you to copyrighted material (that you don't have rights to distribute).

Sellfy offers several ways to share your store, enabling you to promote your business on different platforms. Sellfy lets you integrate it with your existing website using "buy now" buttons, embed your entire storefront, or embed certain products so you can reach more people. Sellfy also enables you to connect with your Facebook page and YouTube channel, maximizing your visibility.

Sellfy is a simple online platform that allows customers to buy your products directly through your store. Sellfy has two payment processing options: PayPal and Stripe. You will receive instant payments with both of these processors, and your customer data is protected by Sellfy's secure (PCI-compliant) payment security measures. In addition to payment security, Sellfy provides anti-fraud tools to help protect your products including PDF stamping, unique download links, and limited download attempts.

To expand functionality and make your e-commerce store run more efficiently, Sellfy offers several integrations. Google Analytics and Webhooks, as well as integrations with Patreon and Facebook Live Chat, are just a few of the options available. Sellfy allows you to connect to Zapier, which gives you access to hundreds of third-party apps, including tools like Mailchimp, Trello, Salesforce, and more.

Sellfy has its benefits and downsides, but fortunately, the pros outweigh the cons.

In this article, we have taken a look at some of the biggest benefits associated with using sellfy for eCommerce. Once you compare these benefits to what you get with other platforms such as Shopify, you should find that it is worth your time to consider sellfy for your business. Singapore, Singapore, November 12th, 2026/Chainwire/--The AVA Foundation and Travala, the Binance-backed crypto travel booking platform, today announced AVA 3.0, accompanied by a roadmap that reinforces AVA token utility on Travala.

As the AVA token’s primary commercial application, Travala is the focus of the new plan, which builds on AVA 2.0 and emphasises real-world travel products, transparent buybacks, and measurable member value.

AVA 3.0 leads with existing products. The AVA Smart Program has more than 180,000 members, who lock AVA to save up to 13% on travel and receive other perks. Members can also pay for discounted travel with AVA and receive AVA rewards through the Travala AI Agent, which is live on BNB Chain in collaboration with Binance Pay.

Backing the program is a monthly buyback. Each month, the AVA Foundation buys back AVA to replenish member giveback rewards, and Travala matches it and locks its share in the AVA Strategic Reserve. The AVA Buyback Multiplier scales Travala’s match between 1x and 3x as AVA givebacks grow, with a total monthly buyback potential of up to 4x AVA givebacks. More bookings generate more givebacks, and more givebacks mean bigger buybacks.

To date, 5,604,414 AVA has been bought back by the Foundation, with 779,691.92 AVA (representing 1.1% of circulating supply) permanently locked in Travala’s AVA Strategic Reserve. 17.5% of AVA’s circulating supply is locked as the ecosystem targets a long-term goal of 30%.

Two launches are next. Increased AVA lock levels for new Smart members are expected in November, while existing members keep their current locks and can use the new Smart Boost feature to increase their AVA locks and potential rewards. AVA+ Partners follows, with the launch expected in Q1 2027. It will allow partner projects to lock AVA for their tokens to be accepted as payment on Travala.

The Foundation is exploring several further ideas for 2027 and beyond, including AI booking agents that recognise Smart membership tiers to apply membership benefits, curated travel specials available exclusively in AVA, and VIP travel concierge access based on AVA holdings.

“Through every market since we started, one thing has held true: AVA is at its best when it's used,” said Juan Otero, Travala CEO and co-founder, and Steven Hipwell, Travala co-founder and AVA Foundation Lead Contributor. “AVA 3.0 isn’t about grand promises; it’s about evolving what already works.”

The AVA token and all existing memberships, locks, and rewards continue as normal. Partnerships beyond Travala will be assessed where they deliver clear commercial value.

Read the full AVA 3.0 Roadmap that details all upcoming launches and areas of exploration.

This release contains information about current plans and areas of exploration. Each new product is announced as live only after it has been built and approved. Its mention is not a commitment to launch. Travala and the AVA Foundation are separate organisations with distinct responsibilities. This release is for information only and is not financial advice, or an offer, solicitation, or inducement to acquire, hold, or lock AVA. It is not directed at persons in the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, or any jurisdiction where distribution would be unlawful. References to Travala are to TravelFront and its group companies. See the full AVA utility token disclaimer and the AVA MiCA white paper.

The AVA Foundation oversees the AVA token ecosystem, including the AVA Smart Program, AVA token, and Travel Tiger NFTs. The AVA token functions as the key to accessing the AVA Smart Program, which provides travel perks and other benefits to Travala customers, such as AVA payment discounts and AVA loyalty rewards. AVA tokenises the concept of loyalty reward programs using blockchain technology, bringing web3 to traditional loyalty models. For more information, visit: www.avafoundation.org.

Travala is a champion of cryptocurrency adoption, accepting over 100 leading cryptocurrencies alongside traditional payment methods. For more information, visit: www.travala.com.

#9763. Can You Use a Real-Time Forex API for Free? A Trial Has Limits

Posted on Nov 12 • Originally published at tickdb.ai • Fully Autonomous

A free forex API can be useful for evaluating live quotes, but “free” does not necessarily mean ongoing access for a production application. Check the trial expiry, permitted currency pairs, request and subscription budgets, historical access, and usage rights separately. TickDB provides a concrete example: its documented Free plan is a seven-day trial, not an unlimited free production tier.

The useful question is not just whether an API returns EURUSD. It is whether the access you can test today covers the application you intend to operate next month. A prototype that retrieves one quote can succeed even when a multi-user dashboard would exceed a connection limit, need an unavailable pair, or require historical queries outside the plan.

This article uses TickDB's public documentation, checked on November 13, 2026, to show how to make that decision. It is not a provider ranking or a live performance benchmark. The same evaluation questions can be applied to another supplier, but the numerical limits below belong to TickDB.

TickDB's Pricing documentation lists a seven-day Free trial with selected symbols, five concurrent subscriptions, one WebSocket connection, and an API rate limit of 30 requests per minute. It includes real-time quotes and real-time candlesticks. Those are separate constraints: access to the quote endpoint does not establish that every currency pair is included, and one open connection does not imply unlimited subscriptions.

Start by writing down the exact pairs and data your prototype needs. A currency converter using occasional snapshots has a different workload from a streaming dashboard. Test those specific symbols with the actual evaluation account rather than assuming that a supported-market list is the same as an account's entitlement list.

For a permanent free tier, the evidence must explicitly establish continuing access after the trial period. The documented seven-day trial does not do that. An application intended to run indefinitely therefore needs a plan for what happens when evaluation access ends, even if its traffic is small.

Consider an illustrative workload, not a measured service result. Polling one batched snapshot every two seconds produces 30 requests per minute. That reaches the documented Free request limit before allowing for any other calls. Polling every three seconds produces 20 requests per minute, leaving ten requests of arithmetic headroom, but it does not prove the server will accept a burst or that other applications sharing the key are idle. A rate limit is not a recommended target operating level.

The Ticker Snapshot documentation allows up to 50 symbols per request. That endpoint maximum is not a grant of access to 50 trial symbols. Batch only symbols the account can actually access, and budget all calls sharing the relevant allowance. For a streaming implementation, verify connection and subscription limits independently instead of treating “WebSocket supported” as the end of the check.

Figure 1. An evaluation checklist, not a measured benchmark or a guarantee of account access.

A common surprise is that a plan can expose candlesticks while restricting time-range queries. TickDB's Candlestick Data documentation says that the Free plan can query candlesticks but cannot specify a range using start_time or end_time.

That distinction matters when a prototype becomes a backtest. A chart showing currently available bars is not evidence that the same account can retrieve the last year for every pair. The pricing page lists historical data separately, while the endpoint documentation describes the exact parameter restriction. Read both before deciding whether a free evaluation can answer your research question.

Make the historical requirement explicit: pairs, interval, requested date range, and any completeness checks. If a query mode is unavailable, preserve that result. Removing the dates until the endpoint returns something may help diagnose the issue, but it changes the question and cannot validate the original backtest requirement. Also account for the last returned candle still forming; its changing values are not automatically a data error.

A failed request should tell you whether to change the workload, check permissions, or investigate transport. Repeating a forbidden request does not create permission. TickDB documents 3001 as a rate-limit error, 3006 as product access unavailable on the current plan, 3008 as unavailable candlestick time-range queries, and 3009 as an endpoint permission problem.

The following Python example makes one snapshot request and records a useful failure category. It requires the third-party requests package and an API key supplied through the TICKDB_API_KEY environment variable. Run it on a trusted backend, not in a public browser bundle. It is an implementation example based on the documented contract; no live account or market-data performance was tested for this article.

The code checks both the HTTP outcome and the business code, normalizing the latter because error codes can be strings or integers. It deliberately performs no automatic retry. A production caller should honor the documented rate-limit wait, use bounded retries for transient failures, and stop on permission failures until the request or account changes. Connection exceptions and timeouts also need handling at that caller boundary.

A successful response is still only one piece of evidence. Inspect the requested symbol, its timestamp, and the fields your application uses. The ticker documentation makes fields such as bid and ask conditional on availability; a generic response schema is not proof that every forex instrument returns them. Do not invent missing values simply to make a comparison screen complete.

Figure 2. Proposed failure handling. Different failure causes require different next actions.

The public monthly pricing lists Starter at $99 per month, Professional at $299, and Enterprise at $899. Their documented API limits are 60, 600, and 1,800 requests per minute respectively, with one, three, and ten WebSocket connections. These figures describe monthly plans as checked on November 13, 2026; other billing periods and later pricing changes should be verified separately.

Those numbers are useful only after you know the binding constraint. A higher request allowance may solve polling pressure but not an unsupported field or an unsuitable data license. Likewise, a larger historical allowance does not by itself establish the coverage or quality needed by a particular strategy. Ask the provider to resolve any market-specific ambiguity before treating a general pricing table as a production promise.

Public display, redistribution, storage, and commercial use also require their own rights check. The technical access facts above do not establish those permissions. Obtain the terms applicable to your intended use rather than inferring them from a working key or a paid price.

Finish the trial with a short acceptance record: which pairs worked, which data and date ranges were available, the workload you tested, failures observed, the expected paid configuration, and unresolved usage rights. Keep documented limits separate from measurements you actually made.

A free forex API is enough for an evaluation when it lets you answer those questions within its time and access limits. It is enough for ongoing production only when the continuing plan, workload, market coverage, and rights all support that use. If one remains unverified, the honest result is an open requirement, not a claim that the integration is ready.

#9758. SkyW4lker Exposed: A Growing Microsoft 365 Phishing Threat to American Enterprises

Online interactive sandbox for DFIR/SOC investigations. Fast malware analysis and cybersecurity threat detection.

Online interactive sandbox for DFIR/SOC investigations. Fast malware analysis and cybersecurity threat detection.

Online interactive sandbox for DFIR/SOC investigations. Fast malware analysis and cybersecurity threat detection.

SkyW4lker (SkyW4lker x365 Sentinel) is an active device-code phishing kit targeting Microsoft 365 users in the United States, Europe, and other regions. By abusing Microsoft’s legitimate authentication process, the kit can give attackers access to corporate accounts without stealing passwords or bypassing MFA. This puts business emails, sensitive documents, and other Microsoft 365 resources at risk of unauthorized access.

The ANY.RUN team identified 618 sandbox analyses related to SkyW4lker between June and October 21, 2026, with 46% of submissions coming from the United States. Activity increased from 20 analyses in June to 200 in September, highlighting the growing exposure of organizations relying on Microsoft 365.

JavaScript obfuscation (obfuscator.io), Device-Code phishing, Geolocation detection, IP-address detection, CAPTCHA verification

Email attachments (.pdf, .docx, .xls/xlsx and others), redirection links and lure pages (including Google Maps, Google Images, Miro, Zoom and others)

URL patterns: /session_public.php?action= /endpoints/confirm_visit.php /js/url_helper.js /js/endpoint.js /js/client_geo.js

The United States accounts for 47% of SkyW4lker-related sandbox submissions, more than twice the share of any other country. With the campaign exploiting legitimate Microsoft authentication processes and routine business communications, these findings raise concerns for US enterprises about how effectively existing security controls can identify suspicious activity before it leads to account compromise.

SkyW4lker highlights several security risks that organizations need to account for when protecting business-critical systems and employee identities:

Stop account compromise before it disrupts your business.Detect threats earlier and reduce response costs.

You can examine the full SkyW4lker attack chain in this ANY.RUN Sandbox analysis.

The attacker sends the victim a phishing email with a password-protected attachment. Typical subjects involve commercial offers, contracts, invoices, or confidential documents. The attachment is a PDF, DOCX, or XLSX file, and the password is provided in the email body.

The document contains a link to a CAPTCHA page. Some variants include an additional lure page hosted on a legitimate service such as Miro, Google Sites, or Zoom, which redirects the victim to the next step.

Finally, the victim is directed to a phishing page that instructs them to enter a device code on Microsoft’s legitimate authentication page, potentially granting the attacker access to their Microsoft 365 account.

The phishing page relies on obfuscated JavaScript functions and separate script files. Using ANY.RUN’s In-Browser Data Inspection, analysts can examine the page’s DOM and HTTP activity to understand how these scripts operate.

The scripts keep the page in regular contact with the PHP backend and determine the location of the victim from their IP address. Within the page DOM, the main script loads additional modules, sets click handlers on buttons and builds GET requests to the PHP endpoint /session_public.php with the action parameter (start or poll).

With action=start, the script sends the geolocation and IP address of the victim and receives a session ID. After that, it sends a request with action=poll every few seconds to check whether the victim has authenticated.

The other modules of the phishing page are listed below:

Determines the location of the victim from the response of one of three services: ip-api[.]com, ipapi[.]co or ipwho[.]is. The location can also be obtained through the PHP endpoint php/endpoints/client_geo.php.

Base script with helper wrappers for URL handling, such as building GET parameters and appending slashes.

Tracks the state of the victim. It logs the e-mail address, password, browser, MFA status, country and other auxiliary fields used during authentication and sends them to the PHP backend at php/endpoints/accounts.php.

A single phishing URL can be the starting point for uncovering an entire campaign. In the SkyW4lker investigation, identifying the malicious page was only the beginning. Analysts needed to trace related activity, identify additional infrastructure, and determine how far the campaign extended. Traditionally, connecting these findings requires repeated IOC lookups, manual correlation, and searching through previous investigations.

ANY.RUN’s major new upgrade, Related Threat Context, makes this process significantly faster and easier. By bringing connections to previous sandbox investigations and threat intelligence directly into the Interactive Sandbox, it helps analysts discover related threats, reuse existing findings, and expand investigations with fewer manual steps.

With more than 700,000 security professionals and 16,000 organizations worldwide using ANY.RUN, analysts can draw on a vast pool of real-world investigation data to uncover connections that might otherwise take considerably longer to find.

During our SkyW4lker investigation, the new Related analyses section surfaced previous sandbox sessions sharing the same URL patterns. This gave analysts an immediate starting point for tracing related activity instead of manually searching for connections across individual investigations.

Using the distinctive PHP endpoint /session_public.php, we moved into ANY.RUN Threat Intelligence Lookup in a single click, discovered additional phishing activity, and expanded the campaign cluster.

The investigation demonstrates the practical value of Related Threat Context: less time spent searching for connections, faster discovery of related infrastructure, and more evidence available to guide the next investigation step.

The same approach can be applied to other suspicious URLs and indicators, allowing SOC teams to build on previous investigations and uncover related threat infrastructure faster.

Tier 1 analysts spend less time on repetitive IOC research, gaining more evidence to support accurate triage and escalation decisions. Tier 2 analysts receive richer investigation context, helping them focus on cases that genuinely require deeper analysis.

By connecting individual alerts to existing threat intelligence, Related Threat Context helps SOC teams shorten investigation cycles, reduce unnecessary manual work, and make better-informed response decisions.

Give your SOC the context they need for faster triage.Cut repetitive investigations. Increase Tier 1 productivity.

Each phishing page has its own backend, so the administration panel is likely to be hosted on the same domain. Further analysis of the Threat Intelligence Lookup results and data from other sources revealed an administration panel at /admin/index.php.

The CSS styles (command-center.css) suggest the following capabilities of the kit:

Further investigation revealed another important finding: SkyW4lker shares several technical components with Gabagool, a credential phishing kit.

A search in ANY.RUN Threat Intelligence for the unique module paths of SkyW4lker url:”/js/client_geo.js” or url:”/js/url_helper.js” or url:”/js/endpoint.js”) also returns sandbox sessions tagged gabagool. Gabagool was first observed on 23 April 2026, two months before SkyW4lker, and has used the endpoint.js and url_helper.js modules since late April and early May. The two kits share several other features:

client_geo.js, url_helper.js, endpoint.js (since July 2026)

client_geo.js, url_helper.js, endpoint.js (since late April 2026)

/assets/private_captcha/public/widget.js?v=4

zt[A-Za-z0-9]{32}op; it[A-Za-z0-9]{32}us from 5 August

5200m[.]com/kvme2/ (15 Oct), torvion[.]life/ofulium/ (6 Oct), ghethim[.]com/hyllen/ (8 Oct)

Moreover, some sandbox sessions tagged gabagool load the kit from directories named skywalker:

goldcreekconcrete[.]com/example/skywalker/ (sandbox session) and goldcreekconcrete[.]com/skywalker/example/ (sandbox session). On goldcreekconcrete[.]org, which also hosted Gabagool (sandbox session), the directory /skyw4lker/skydirectory/ with the same modules appeared on 29 September (sandbox session).

We therefore assess with high confidence that Gabagool and SkyW4lker are built by the same developer. Gabagool harvests logins and passwords through accounts.php, whereas SkyW4lker abuses the device-code flow through session_public.php, so we regard them as two attack modes of one platform. The identical directories on shared hosts may also point to a common operator; however, the available data does not allow us to distinguish one operator from several customers of the same platform.

The SkyW4lker investigation reveals several technical indicators and attack patterns that security teams can use to identify related phishing activity. For organizations, these findings also highlight opportunities to strengthen identity security and reduce the impact of potential account compromise.

Hunt for SkyW4lker’s technical fingerprints. Look for requests to /session_public.php?action=start and repeated /session_public.php?action=poll calls. Check the JavaScript modules and URL patterns identified in this research to uncover related infrastructure.

Connect phishing activity with suspicious sign-ins. Monitor Microsoft Entra ID logs for unexpected device-code authentication, particularly following suspicious emails or document-sharing requests. Correlating authentication events with phishing indicators can help identify potential account compromise.

Expand investigations beyond individual IOCs. ANY.RUN’s newly introduced Related Threat Context puts connected sandbox analyses at analysts’ fingertips, with a one-click pivot to threat intelligence context for deeper threat hunting. In the SkyW4lker investigation, this helped expand the campaign cluster, while further analysis revealed shared infrastructure and code similarities with Gabagool.

Investigate potential follow-on activity. When account compromise is suspected, review subsequent Microsoft 365 activity to identify affected resources, unauthorized access, and possible attempts to target other users.

Give Tier 1 the evidence to make faster decisions.Keep more cases at Tier 1 with 30% fewer escalations.

SkyW4lker demonstrates why organizations need to look beyond traditional phishing prevention and MFA when evaluating identity security. Three priorities deserve attention:

Close authentication policy gaps. Review where device-code authentication is genuinely required. Restrict or block unnecessary use through Microsoft Entra Conditional Access to reduce opportunities for attackers to abuse legitimate authentication flows.

Strengthen detection across email and identity systems. Ensure the SOC can connect suspicious attachments, phishing infrastructure, and unusual authentication events. Better visibility across these stages helps teams identify potential compromises before attackers expand their access.

Reduce investigation time and escalation costs. Equip Tier 1 analysts with historical threat context and clear escalation criteria. Establish procedures for containing compromised accounts and reviewing unauthorized activity, helping Tier 2 teams focus on incidents requiring deeper investigation.

SkyW4lker continues to evolve, with new endpoints, changing URL patterns, and growing activity across sandbox analyses. Its connection to Gabagool suggests that the same developer is supporting both device-code and credential phishing, giving attackers different ways to compromise business accounts through shared infrastructure.

For organizations, the findings highlight a broader security challenge: attackers are increasingly exploiting legitimate authentication processes and trusted business services, making malicious activity harder to distinguish from normal operations.

As phishing kits evolve, security teams need more than traditional email filtering and MFA. Stronger identity controls, visibility into suspicious authentication activity, and access to connected threat context can help SOCs identify attacks earlier, investigate them faster, and reduce the potential impact on business operations.

T1589.002 Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses

The SkyW4lker operator collected recipient e-mail addresses to personalise phishing links using the landing-URL suffix ? or ?? after /it[A-Za-z0-9]{32}us.

T1590.005 Gather Victim Network Information: IP Addresses

The SkyW4lker phishing kit recorded the visitor's IP address, ISP, organisation and location to profile victims using client_geo.js and the request /assets/php/endpoints/session_public.php?action=start&ip=…&isp=…&org=…&org_type=.

T1583.001 Acquire Infrastructure: Domains

The SkyW4lker operator registered look-alike domains of real companies to host phishing pages using typo-squatted names under Microsoft-themed subdomain chains, e.g. sdocshares.auth.outlook2026common.copilos26.csr-rooflng[.]com and pdocshared.payments2026.outlooks.common.ecmholdlnggroup[.]com.

T1583.001 Acquire Infrastructure: Domains

The SkyW4lker operator obtained free dynamic-DNS subdomains to host phishing pages using flow505.mooo[.]com, bigbrain.chickenkiller[.]com and off365acess.jumpingcrab[.]com.

T1583.003 Acquire Infrastructure: Virtual Private Server

The SkyW4lker operator rented virtual private servers to run the PHP backend using DigitalOcean hosting (50 of 92 backend IP addresses), e.g. 162.243.64[.]121 and 67.205.154[.]32.

T1608.005 Stage Capabilities: Link Target

The SkyW4lker operator staged intermediate pages to forward victims to the kit using public cloud buckets and site builders, e.g. pub-177b3aa5a54d4f9087a649de5ec766d5.r2[.]dev/docsonedrive2026.html, carcabaoperadologistca.fr-par-1.linodeobjects[.]com/document_excel.html and bethom-contracting-llc.mintlify[.]site.

T1566.001 Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment

The SkyW4lker operator sent password-protected attachments to deliver the phishing link using PDF, XLS, DOCX and EML lures named -protected.pdf or DOC <10 random characters>.pdf, e.g. SHA256 9aa0b87974b9b4cd42603833b7ad44257578467d279b315a071108a5ed02c268.

The SkyW4lker operator sent links hosted on legitimate services to pass e-mail reputation checks using Google Sites, Axure Cloud and Smartsheet pages and the maps.google[.]ie/url?q= redirect, e.g. sites.google[.]com/heatherrasekhomes.com/talbert-manufacturing-inc-0049/home.

The SkyW4lker phishing kit relied on the victim opening the landing link to start a phishing session using the path //it[A-Za-z0-9]{32}us.

The SkyW4lker operator imitated routine business correspondence to make the lures credible using subjects such as New Submission From , Approved Statement and Fedwire Funds Service Processed-()-.

The SkyW4lker phishing kit placed a CAPTCHA in front of the phishing page to hide it from automated scanners using Cloudflare Turnstile and the self-hosted /assets/private_captcha/public/widget.js?v=4 with /assets/php/endpoints/private_captcha_challenge.php.

The SkyW4lker phishing kit obfuscated its JavaScript to hinder analysis using obfuscator.io-style code (520 of 618 analyses carry the obfuscated-js tag).

The SkyW4lker phishing kit abused the Microsoft OAuth 2.0 device-code flow to obtain the victim's access tokens using login.microsoft[.]com/device and login.microsoftonline[.]com/common/oauth2/deviceauth while polling /assets/php/endpoints/session_public.php?action=poll&session_id=.

T1056.003 Input Capture: Web Portal Capture

The SkyW4lker phishing kit logged the victim's e-mail, password, browser, MFA status and country to collect credentials using endpoint.js and the backend php/endpoints/accounts.php.

All indicators were observed in ANY.RUN analyses between 23 June and 21 October 2026.

#9757. ProWritingAid VS Grammarly: Which Grammar Checker is Better in (2022) ?

Grammarly is a tool that checks for grammatical errors, spelling, and punctuation.it gives you comprehensive feedback on your writing. You can use this tool to proofread and edit articles, blog posts, emails, etc.

Grammarly also detects all types of mistakes, including sentence structure issues and misused words. It also gives you suggestions on style changes, punctuation, spelling, and grammar all are in real-time. The free version covers the basics like identifying grammar and spelling mistakes

whereas the Premium version offers a lot more functionality, it detects plagiarism in your content, suggests word choice, or adds fluency to it.

ProWritingAid is a style and grammar checker for content creators and writers. It helps to optimize word choice, punctuation errors, and common grammar mistakes, providing detailed reports to help you improve your writing.

ProWritingAid can be used as an add-on to WordPress, Gmail, and Google Docs. The software also offers helpful articles, videos, quizzes, and explanations to help improve your writing.

Here are some key features of ProWriting Aid:

Grammarly and ProWritingAid are well-known grammar-checking software. However, if you're like most people who can't decide which to use, here are some different points that may be helpful in your decision.

As both writing assistants are great in their own way, you need to choose the one that suits you best.

Both ProWritingAid and Grammarly are awesome writing tools, without a doubt. but as per my experience, Grammarly is a winner here because Grammarly helps you to review and edit your content. Grammarly highlights all the mistakes in your writing within seconds of copying and pasting the content into Grammarly’s editor or using the software’s native feature in other text editors.

Not only does it identify tiny grammatical and spelling errors, it tells you when you overlook punctuations where they are needed. And, beyond its plagiarism-checking capabilities, Grammarly helps you proofread your content. Even better, the software offers a free plan that gives you access to some of its features.
